method.value: Jenny ran Muse in the browser, where her Instagram and Threads accounts were already linked. outcome.value: The task was created and the first digest arrived. Jenny found the report general, and she said she barely uses Meta apps, so Muse had little to read.

notes.value: Muse is free. Jenny used the browser version and gave it minimal access because of a reported Mac app Messages-sync problem, which Meta disputes.

source_text.body:
Get a daily digest of top AI-agent posts from social feeds
The author asked Muse to send the 5 best AI-agent posts from their Threads and Instagram feeds each morning at 8; it created a scheduled task and sent a first, general report.
Done with
MM
Meta Muse
What they did
Jenny ran Muse in the browser, where her Instagram and Threads accounts were already linked. She asked in one sentence for the 5 best AI-agent posts from those feeds every morning at 8 for 3 days, with no likes, follows or replies. Muse turned the request into a scheduled task card called "AI agents morning briefing" and sent back a first report.
How it went
The task was created and the first digest arrived. Jenny found the report general, and she said she barely uses Meta apps, so Muse had little to read.
Worth knowing
Muse is free. Jenny used the browser version and gave it minimal access because of a reported Mac app Messages-sync problem, which Meta disputes.
Try it yourself
with
Meta Muse
Copy prompt
Every morning at [8am, my time zone], look through my [Threads and Instagram] feeds and pick the [5] best posts about [topic, e.g. AI agents]. Send me a short digest with a one-line summary of each post and a link, favoring posts with new ideas over general news. Set this up as a recurring scheduled task, run it once now so I can see the format, and ask me before changing anything on my accounts.
Original source: https://buildtolaunch.substack.com/p/chatgpt-dot-vs-grok-bot-vs-meta-muse-use-cases
